content: Hello! my name is Eamon Duede. I'm a professor at Purdue doing research with my postdoc on the use of AI in formalization projects as part of a grant from the Sloan Foundation. The first thing we're trying to do is just compile a list of meaningfully large, ongoing (github) projects that involve the use of AI in some explicit way -whether these are full blown AI authored projects or projects that welcome AI or are leveraging AI to get their work done. If you are aware of / involved with such a project and would like to add it to this list, that would be spectacularly helpful. I plan to keep the list available to the community as it is compiled!

Just to throw out an "obvious" idea, doing a query on repositories tagged with the lean or leanprover tags (or equally reservoir's list), looping over repositories in descending star order or something, and then checking whether any of the last N commits are co-authored by Claude might seed such a list. (EDIT: actually it looks like --language lean exists, so that's an even better way than tags, or could combine with tags).

Another good strategy for finding Lean repositories is checking for the existence of lean-toolchain, lakefile.toml or lakefile.lean files. In my experience sometimes this finds stuff that Github's language detection doesn't.
We added a tab to the sheet called 'lean repos' w/ about 2,400 repos using the loop strategies @Julian Berman and @Kim Morrison suggested.
